body: In y 900-1500 the only non-periodic events are: (1) the people-o reset when #future-heading leaves the top (y 920 at vh815, 1020 at vh932, ~28 layouts/step, 6 face + grid/height transitions); (2) .pain gets is-pain-dark (y<900 at vh815, 980 at vh932); (3) the .commission.compact scene gate paused->active (IO rootMargin 100%, y 1340 at BOTH viewports, because commission top - 2vh = 1330 = .pain top). Every deferred section was already render=active at y=0 (the /10 idle pre-unskip ran during the settle), and there were no contentvisibilityautostatechange events, so a render un-skip does not cause the y~1250 frame. Avatar carousel ticks are periodic, not y-locked. The commission gate is the only y-locked event near 1250. It clears animation-play-state:paused and will-change:auto on the whole 1203 px subtree in one frame, so it restarts the three-frame-zero / orbit animations and promotes layers. That costs little in Chrome (S12 L1) but is plausibly a layer burst in WebKit. Mapping to the phone: y = 1330 + 2*(lvh - innerHeight) = 1330-1410 if the phone's document matches Chrome@815, or about 1250-1330 if the phone document is ~77 px shorter above .pain. title: WebKit 26.6: a style change that flips opacity <1 to 1, filter none to some, or transform none to some (either way) is a Layout diff up to the first layout boundary; a finished transition or GraphicsL
evidence: phone P3: re-dur shifts the +700 Layout, re-keep removes +900/+1150 (OBSERVED, n=2 per arm)
body: Accelerated opacity/transform: no per-frame style; at the end the Stop action calls invalidateStyleAndLayerComposition (KeyframeEffect.cpp l.2429-2434) and the recalc diffs the animated value against 1/none: a flip, so Layout. Main-thread filter: each frame is a Filter change (RepaintLayer/RecompositeLayer); the end blur to none flips. No flip, no Layout: translateY(0) to scale(1) is RecompositeLayer (composited) or Overflow (layer, not composited). Layer gain/loss adds Layout (adjustStyleDifference l.351-355) but never forces a full layout; the root is the first isLayoutBoundary (RenderObject.cpp l.523-562, 598-660). re-keep-op (opacity 0.999) avoids the flip. Risk UNRESOLVED: a non-composited opacity<1 layer paints through beginTransparencyLayer on every repaint (RenderLayerInlines.h l.70-75, RenderLayer.cpp l.2711-2737); iOS has no FilterTrigger (WebChromeClient.h l.292-306); blur(0px) is an identity filter and is not painted (RenderLayer.cpp l.1017-1027). claims-audit section 2.8.

title: iOS: non-passive touchmove gates only the pan start (once per touch sequence), not each move (C1 CONFIRMED); touch event.timeStamp UNRESOLVED (C2)
evidence: WebKit-7624.4.5: Quirks.cpp 983-1008 + EventTarget.cpp 100-104 (root-target touch listeners passive unless {passive:false}); WebPageProxy.cpp 4711-4734, 4764-4765, 4779-4797, 4803-4804 (async-with-reply, Waiting set once per sequence); WKContentViewInteraction.mm 2242-2248, 4174-4181, 10484-10485 (deferrer holds pan/pinch until first reply; after pan starts all moves unpreventable); TouchEvent.h 29-30 (iOS TouchEvent in closed WebKitAdditions)
body: C1: a window touchmove listener without explicit {passive:false} is passive and never waits. With {passive:false}, only the FIRST preventable touchmove of a touch sequence gates the scroll start (UIPan/UIPinch deferred until the web process replies); once the pan begins, later moves go async and nothing waits per move. Expect a C-vs-V difference in touch-to-scroll-start only; handler work still costs frames like any main-thread work. Whether later moves have cancelable=false in the DOM is UNRESOLVED (log e.cancelable per move). C2: Event.timeStamp = m_createTime (Event.cpp 188-199), but the iOS TouchEvent constructor is closed source, so platform-stamp vs creation-at-dispatch is UNRESOLVED. Decisive check: log performance.now()-e.timeStamp with and without a 50 ms busy loop that ends while a touch is pending; ~0-2 ms both ways = creation at dispatch, +tens of ms = earlier stamp.

title: I-032 opt-in render signals (main 2f81a3e): --trace-frames presentation/layer split, --trace-phases, --save-trace, --paint-rects, longFrames >34 ms, bench kind layers
where: tools/verify.mjs header L41-65; lib/trace-frames.mjs, lib/paint-rects.mjs, lib/frame-tags.mjs
evidence: review-render-signals ACCEPT; npm test 768/768; test:chrome paint test 142 of 417 scroll frames painted at layerScale 2
body:
All flags are opt-in. A default run is byte-identical (golden CDP sequence). Pass them to verify.mjs or fix.mjs ab; ab writes paint results to results-paint.json and leaves results.json untouched.
(1) --trace-frames now also records: DroppedFrame / partial frames from the Frames track, BeginFrame/DrawFrame, layerMs (Layerize/UpdateLayer/Composite/Commit, a sub-split of paintMs) and Paint event counts. --trace-phases idle,scroll,morph traces several phases (default: scroll). --save-trace writes each trace for the DevTools Performance panel: about 200-300 MB EACH, and verify prints the file count first. Tracing perturbs timing: traced numbers compare only within one A/B with the same trace-phase set and tool version.
(2) --paint-rects: CDP LayerTree in every phase.
- Records per frame: paints, layer count, added/removed layers. Per layer: paint counts, plus the DOM node and compositing reasons of the top layers.
- On Chrome 148+ the source is paintCount rises (layerPainted is dead, CONFIRMED F-064), so mpx (dirty-clip area) is null. layerMpx / layerVpMpx are upper bounds (full or viewport-capped painted-layer size).
- UNITS: layer px = CSS px x the HOST display DSF, not the emulated DPR 3 (CONFIRMED F-077). Recorded as paintRects.layerScale and measurement.paintLayerScales. Mixed scales (e.g. external display) get the tag PAINT-SCALE-MIXED.
- Overhead: scroll fps 86.6 -> 66.6 in an on/off A/A, so use it for ATTRIBUTION ONLY. Compare only with other --paint-rects runs at the same layerScale, never as a gain A/B.
(3) longFrames: with --frame-log, --trace-frames or --paint-rects, run.longFrames.<phase> lists every frame >34 ms. Each entry has ticks, scrollY (--frame-log only), trace class, top LoAF script, paint area / top layer and layer delta.
(4) bench probe kind 'layers' counts paintCount rises.
Caveats:
N1: the Frames-track dropped/partial counts are NOT filtered to the main layerTreeId or to frameSeqId (DevTools does both). See byLayerTree in the output.
N7: whether LayerTree.enable changes bench perfMetrics is UNRESOLVED, and bench window fuzz is unmeasured. Bench stores nothing from layers, so treat its counts as mechanism checks only.

body: Overlay files keep the baseline's hashed immutable name, so Safari on the Sim (cache persists across sim.mjs sessions) treats them as the same immutable resource per origin (localhost:<port>). serve.mjs --port auto hands the same ports to different overlays across sessions. Effect: an arm's CSS-only change can be missing (or a baseline page can get an arm's CSS). Check: computed style of a property your CSS changes, plus the server log for a GET of your CSS. Workaround until a tool fix: serve each overlay on an origin Safari has never cached (a fresh port per session), or make the check fail loudly. A real fix probably belongs in sim.mjs (clear Safari website data at session start) or serve.mjs (no immutable cache-control for overlay files): lead's call.

body: (1) fix-nav-morph, cdwc: with cd-strip there are no .face spans, so cdwc's panel .face rule (CSS 11953) matches nothing. Arm (b) ships its own retarget, .start-selling-morph-panel .waitlist-closing-countdown .strip.svelte-1quva9c { will-change: auto }, which keeps the panel clock unlayered as on st6-rb2. Keep or drop the dead .face rule as you like. (2) fix-cd-roll-ca: __cdStripY(v, c) = -(((v % 10) + 10) % 10) * c is periodic, so it jumps from -9.99c to 0 when v crosses a multiple of 10. A driver that animates the strip (WAAPI keyframes) must keep offsets in that one period (linear -v*c for v in [0, 9]) and never interpolate across v = 0 mod 10 through the modulo. Cell 10 (a second 0 at 10c) is a guard only and never shows with this spring. (3) illusion-digit-layers (.face will-change: auto, stacked on B) is superseded for the countdown: cd-strip replaces the 10 faces per digit with one strip, and countdown-faces part (a) with it. countdown-faces part (b) (hidden gate) needs a restack on cd-strip: its patch.diff is against the plain baseline and rewrites the same $E body.

title: A per-frame rAF integrator becomes a time-based WAAPI path that is exact at every 60 Hz frame of any phase: sample GE(x mod T) + whole frames from 33 phase lanes
evidence: fixes/cd-roll-ca/results.json positions: 0.13-0.15 px max vs the original at 60 Hz (uniform 240 Hz grid: 0.23 / 2.07 px)
body: Value the original shows at time x after a change, at a 60 Hz frame landing exactly at x = GE(x mod T) then whole T steps. Quadratic in the phase on [kT,kT+16]: 33 lanes, adaptive points (5e-4 cell), 144-343 keyframes, easing keyword linear. Pitfall: when the change lands after a frame began, the original's first rAF stamp is earlier than the change and its clock restarts there; one rAF per roll moves startTime to it (without it: 4.5 px). At 120 Hz the original takes another path (up to 29.5 px), a time-based animation can't follow.

title: WebKit: cover a new scroll-driven animation's pending first frame with an inline value written in the scroll event (or before it), then add the class

body: A newly added scroll-driven animation draws nothing in its first frame (pending). The scroll event fires before that frame's rendering update, so a passive scroll handler that writes the inline value for the current scrollY (no layout read) and adds the animating class makes that frame correct; the animation overrides the inline value from the next frame. The same inline value held at rest (class dropped 300 ms after the last scroll frame) keeps an always-attached transform animation from raising ancestor-dependent repaints (F-160). title: New lock and idle-alarm rules from I-160, I-155, I-165 and phone-hold v2 T0 (once landed)
body:
After the ts-lock-rules series lands (I-160, I-155, I-165, phone-hold v2 T0):
(1) Phone block runner: `lock.mjs doing iphone --owner <you> --block <ticket>` at the block start; `--between <min>` after each hold; `--block none` (or release) at the end. While a block is marked, Simulator sessions print DEFERRED and start only in a window that fits.
(2) Not ready yet for the phone: `lock.mjs acquire iphone --owner <you> --not-ready` keeps your queue place without being served (exit 3; re-run within 10 min). Acquire without the flag when you can start.
(3) Phone-side work that is not a phone run (xctrace gate, pre-warm): wrap it in `lock.mjs run iphone --owner <you> -- <cmd>` under your lease, so it counts as use.
(4) `lock.mjs wait <lock> --until mine` ends as soon as the lock is yours; `--for` is ignored there. A holder whose only process on the iPhone lease is a `lock.mjs wait iphone` for over 2 min is STUCK (an alarm).
(5) Holding chrome-measure counts as phone use. Only being QUEUED for it does not: after 5 min of that wait, while others wait for the phone, the holder gets an IDLE alarm. Release the phone, or queue with --not-ready, until your Mac hold comes.
(6) A holder whose own console step waits for the user's Start (part loading or ready) is not idle.
Idle alarms now put a red alert on the /status rows they concern, and the watch logs NOTIFY <agent> lines.

title: Safari toolbar resize: keep the nav hit-test geometry, defer the re-measure past the frame (no forced layout in iE)
evidence: Simulator WDA finger strokes (out/cm/open0-1.log): every menu-open frame after a toolbar move has the stack getBoundingClientRect, __nsMeasure, _, L, iE: 22-30 ms forced layout (5 of 5 in C and in v12); phone P-159 open-0 frames: 13-15 ms forced layout in iE. tbar-sim: over 13 toolbar moves (innerHeight 775 to 815 and back) scrollHeight, .fw-ms-end (100lvh) and every theme-section edge stayed equal. Page-wide version for the nav-hit-cache owner: valid wherever the cached document offsets do not depend on innerHeight. In Safari vh and lvh stay constant across toolbar moves, dvh and svh do not; so keep the geometry when only innerHeight changed (width equal) and nothing above the probe is sized in dvh or svh (else re-measure as today); the hero pill formula reads innerHeight directly (__nsVh, already updated in the handler). body: Deck: container-type: inline-size (WebKit adds only style + inline-size containment, StyleComputedStyle.cpp 458-468). Shell: drop aspect-ratio, height: calc(100cqi * H / W). title: Preloading (decoding) images ahead moves their paint into the reveal frame: on the iPhone the people reveal frame grew +6-9 ms Paint / +6-12 ms Composite (dt 35-47 -> 44-60 ms)
evidence: P-174 Timeline, 4 runs per arm, FLICK and APPROACH reveal frames
body: Eager + decode() of hidden content makes the first frame that shows it paint and upload all of it at once; lazy content spreads that cost over later frames (and shows blank). Within the no-worse limit here (d +1), but worth knowing for any 'preload so the reveal is complete' fix: consider letting the hidden layer paint ahead (not opacity 0) so the reveal only composites. Also: decode() ahead changed Chrome desktop resampling by up to 0.8 % pixels (fixed in g0.0l rev 2 by limiting the preload to touch screens).

title: WebKit: an element hidden by visibility:hidden gets no backing store; opacity 0 + will-change: opacity keeps it painted while invisible, so a later reveal is composite-only
evidence: RenderLayer::computeHasVisibleContent; RenderLayerBacking::containsPaintedContent -> Styleable::mayHaveNonZeroOpacity (WebKit main 8f0a69f19a28; device branch unread, I-261). Simulator knock-out L+I+W: flip-frame allocation 41 MB -> 0
body: Both halves needed: visibility visible alone (V) still allocates at the flip. Cost: the layers hold memory from load or from entering the coverage rect (~22 MB at the top on g0.0m), and the paint moves to the frames where the layer enters coverage (during a flick: 1-3 frames before the reveal), not to rest. A11y: opacity 0 does not hide from AT.

title: A CSS visibility transition delay wins over an injected !important rule: transitions run above !important in the cascade, so a knock-out stays hidden for the delay
evidence: rp-sim knock-out V: computed visibility still hidden right after injection; settle raised to 2.5 s
body: CSS Cascade 4: transition declarations are in the origin above !important author ones. When injecting a knock-out on a property with a delayed transition, also set transition: none or wait out the delay before you check computed style.

title: WebKit: toggling inert repaints every painting descendant (an effectiveInert change is a Repaint diff), so inert cannot replace visibility: hidden on a pre-painted, opacity-0 layer
evidence: Simulator knock-out N (inert on the hidden #people card, cleared at the flip): both deck shells (402x857) repaint in the flip frame, 2 of 2; flip area 1581-1590 kpx2 vs 1017-1025 for aria-hidden + tabindex (Z) and 608-1017 for g0.0m alone (sessions s12/s13)
body: To keep a visibility: visible + opacity 0 element out of AT and focus without a repaint at the reveal, use attributes no selector reads (aria-hidden on the hidden branches, tabindex -1 on focusables, own values restored; WebKit AttributeChangeInvalidation.cpp 44-80 only invalidates attributes named in rules). Mind descendants with their own visibility rule (here .start-selling-profile-tabs): they were never hidden with the parent, so exclude them (fixes/g0-0m rev 3).
